cohort: 53 COVID-19-negative pregnant women who had delivered between January 1, 2021 and August 31, 2021 and had tested positive for SARS-CoV-2 in the antenatal period
finding: Pregnant women infected with SARS-CoV-2 usually had no/mild symptoms, recovered well, and had favorable maternal and neonatal outcomes, although perinatal vigilance was advisable due to a risk of respiratory morbidity.
mod_finding: The most common indications for cesarean section were fetal distress (17%), previous cesarean section (17%), and unwillingness for vaginal delivery.
